target.title: fix(ui): preserve sidebar session list on Gateway disconnect
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When the Gateway disconnects, `app-sidebar.ts` immediately clears `sessionRowsByAgent` and `sessionCreatedOrder`, causing the entire sidebar session list to disappear. The Gateway reconnect/refresh path will eventually repopulate the list via `context.sessions.subscribe`, but during the disconnect window users see a blank sidebar with no sessions and no explanation. The sessions-page (right panel) does not have this problem — it preserves its last-known data and only shows a "Gateway disconnected" banner. ## Why This Change Was Made The unconditional clear in `updateGatewayClient` is unnecessary: the sessions subscription already handles refreshing rows when Gateway reconnects. Clearing on every client change actively harms UX by hiding valid cached data. Changed to only reset on first connect (`gatewayClient === null && client !== null`) — the one case where stale pre-connection state should be discarded. ## User Impact During Gateway disconnects, the sidebar session list stays visible with the last-loaded result instead of going blank. The list refreshes automatically when the Gateway reconnects. ## Evidence **Before:** `pkill gateway` → sidebar sessions immediately disappear → user sees empty list. **After:** `pkill gateway` → sidebar sessions persist → disconnect banner appears at top → reconnect → subscription refreshes normally. ## Root Cause `updateGatewayClient()` unconditionally clears `sessionRowsByAgent` on every client change, including disconnect. The Gateway session subscribe callback is the proper source of data refresh. The explicit clear in `updateGatewayClient` is redundant for correctness and harmful for UX.
